title: Atlas Core provider certification security assessment
scope: Provider manifests, static readiness, local sandbox conformance, SDK, Gateway authorization, and operator display

prohibited_actions: Represent local conformance as vendor certification

threats.name: Certification triggers an external action
threats.control: Dynamic conformance requires an offline, credential-free, synthetic local-sandbox manifest; remote transport rejects dynamic requests.

threats.name: Manifest becomes a secret or endpoint transport
threats.control: Manifest validation accepts hostnames only when networked and receipts omit endpoint hosts; secrets, URLs, and paths are not contract fields.

threats.name: Runtime capabilities exceed the reviewed manifest
threats.control: Static checks compare provider identity, action allowlists, rollback support, credential strategy, and live-action posture.

threats.name: Conformance leaves synthetic state behind
threats.control: Fixtures use a dedicated atlas-cert tenant prefix and cleanup is checked in a finally path.

threats.name: Static readiness is mistaken for production approval
threats.control: Networked sandboxes remain ready-for-conformance and production manifests always return production-review-required.

threats.name: Readiness leaks exception or provider details
threats.control: Receipts contain bounded check summaries and exception class only, with no raw exception text, credentials, endpoints, or payloads.

findings.finding: The Hotel PMS sandbox passes isolated execute, replay, rollback, restoration, rollback replay, and cleanup checks.
No vendor sandbox or production provider is certified; each requires explicit authorization, credential custody, network controls, and focused review.

validation: Fresh core, SDK, Gateway, and Operator wheels installed with no broken requirements.
Installed remote SDK returned static Hotel PMS sandbox readiness without triggering conformance.
Local conformance returned sandbox-certified and removed its isolated fixture.
residual_risk: This is a conformance framework, not a third-party certification authority.
Manifest assertions require independent review before production use.
No live provider endpoint, credential, data, or action was used.
